chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and are steadfast.
He has authority only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate partners with him.

key_terms.تَعَمَّدُوا: Were steadfast, resolute, or made a conscious choice
key_terms.يَتَوَّلَوْنَهُ: Take him as an ally or guardian

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this verse to refute the Mu'tazila and Khawarij extremes, establishing that Satan's *slutān* (authority) is conditional upon human choice rather than predestined compulsion. This distinction underscores the Shia doctrine of *Amr bayn al-amrayn* (between the two matters), affirming that while believers are susceptible to whispers, they retain the agency to resist through conscious adherence to divine guidance.
